analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation edit to the gpt_oss row of the supported model_type table in docs/architecture/inference.md (line 1163). It states that a bf16 checkpoint keeps bf16 activations and native K/V on every layer, because the expert SwiGLU clamps with scalar bounds that take the activation dtype (GPTOSS+Experts.swift, `swiglu`). It touches no code, configuration, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization or cache-storage behavior. The units I examined are base-text excerpts of the surrounding document (lines 808-1586). Their content (MTP upgrade, prefix cache, MiMo native paths, invariants) is unchanged by the patch. I found no new attack surface and no invalidated assumptions for TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011 or the T-041 prefix-cache threat. The cache-identity and SSD-encryption statements are untouched, and the new sentence does not alter cache TTL, HMAC lookup tags, salt scoping or the SEC-035 accepted risk. The new claim about dtype-dependent kernel behavior is a runtime-correctness assertion. I could not verify it against the source files it cites, and it is not security-relevant on the evidence supplied. The edit cites paths I could not see (libs/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLLM/Models/GPTOSS+Experts.swift), so the claim is unverified, but that does not make it a security regression. No threat-model update is needed from this change.
